attacker_pocs.name: newbug
attacker_pocs.why: The new META_CLASS branch in get_branchlength balances nested extended-class metas by incrementing its depth counter on any meta in the range META_CLASS..META_CLASS_NOT. That range also contains META_CLASS_EMPTY and META_CLASS_EMPTY_NOT, which are self-closing (they have no matching META_CLASS_END). When an extended class inside a lookbehind contains an empty nested class, e.g. (?<=[a[]])x, the counter is incremented with no balancing END, so the scan never reaches depth 0 and runs past the end of the parsed-pattern buffer, dereferencing *pptr out of bounds. The parent lacks this balancing scan and simply computes the length via parsed_skip, so it compiles the pattern without any out-of-bounds access.

role_a_rationale: Task completed: with PCRE2_ALT_EXTENDED_CLASS a fixed-length nested extended class such as (?<=[a[b]])x previously failed with error 125 (length of lookbehind assertion is not limited) because get_branchlength, while computing the fixed length of a lookbehind branch, skipped a class with parsed_skip(PSKIP_CLASS), which stops at the FIRST META_CLASS_END and therefore mis-handles nested classes. The patch makes get_branchlength balance the nesting for extended classes (CLASS_IS_ECLASS), so nested classes compile and still contribute a fixed length of 1. The full test suite (RunTest, RunGrepTest, pcre2posix_test) passes under ASan, and (?<=[a[b]])x, (?<=[a[^b]])x and (?<=[[a-z]&&[^c]])x now compile and match. The new defect is an organic bug in the balancing predicate: the depth counter is bumped for the contiguous meta range META_CLASS..META_CLASS_NOT, idiomatic of range checks used elsewhere in this file, but that range silently includes the two self-closing empty-class metas (META_CLASS_EMPTY, META_CLASS_EMPTY_NOT) which sit numerically between META_CLASS and META_CLASS_NOT. Only a rarely-used shape -- an empty nested class (requiring PCRE2_ALLOW_EMPTY_CLASS) inside a lookbehind -- triggers the unbalanced count and the resulting out-of-bounds read; all ordinary nested/negated classes behave correctly, so the change reads as a plausible, mergeable length-computation fix on commit-by-commit review.
